cohort: A cohort of pregnant females aged 18-49 years, with and without Myasthenia Gravis, and their linked infant records, identified from United States health insurance claims databases between 2000-2023.
finding: Myasthenia Gravis was associated with a greater prevalence of preeclampsia, Cesarean section, preterm birth, and small for gestational age, and many patients with MG did not receive treatment during the perinatal period.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was more frequent in pregnancies with Myasthenia Gravis (42.9%) compared to the age-adjusted total population (36.7%).
birth_weight: Small for gestational age babies were included in the study outcomes, implying birth weight was considered in relation to gestational age.
gest_age: Preterm birth and small for gestational age were measured outcomes, indicating gestational age was a key variable in the study.
